headline: Profit jumps on trading swing, operating earnings dip
summary_short: DTE Energy's Q2 FY2026 GAAP earnings rose 22.7% y/y to $282M ($1.35 diluted EPS), but operating (non-GAAP) earnings of $274M ($1.32/share) were down from $283M ($1.36/share) a year earlier.
summary_long: GAAP net income rose 22.7% y/y to $282M ($1.35 diluted EPS, also $1.35 basic) and 13.4% q/q from $1.19. The GAAP gain is largely a mark-to-market effect: Energy Trading's pretax fair-value adjustment was only $10M unfavorable this quarter versus $54M unfavorable in Q2 2025, which had depressed last year's reported result. On the operating (non-GAAP) basis management uses for guidance, EPS was $1.32, down from $1.36 a year earlier, as DTE Electric segment operating earnings fell to $270M from $318M and DTE Gas slipped to a small operating loss of $4M. DTE confirmed FY2026 operating EPS guidance of $7.59-$7.73, unchanged from the prior range.

drivers.explanation: GAAP diluted EPS rose y/y mainly because Energy Trading's mark-to-market fair-value adjustment was only $10M unfavorable this quarter vs $54M unfavorable in Q2 2025, which had depressed last year's reported result; operating (non-GAAP) EPS of $1.32 was actually down from $1.36.

DTE Electric segment operating earnings fell to $270M from $318M and DTE Gas slipped to a small operating loss; DTE Vantage and Energy Trading operating earnings improved, partially offsetting the utility segments' decline.
